item.title: Claude Pirate: Abusing Anthropic's File API, For Data Exfiltration
item.description:
Author: wunderwuzzi
Date: Oct 28, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Data Exfiltration", "Prompt Injection", "Anthropic Claude", "Cybersecurity Exploits"]
Summary:
  • Anthropic added network requests to Claude's Code Interpreter.
  • This feature can be abused for data exfiltration.
  • Attackers can upload user data to their own Anthropic account.
  • The exploit uses the Files API and indirect prompt injection.
  • Claude resists simple payloads but can be tricked with benign code.
  • The attack can leak up to 30MB of data per file.

item.title: The Backbone Breaker Benchmark: Testing the Real Security of AI Agents
item.description:
Author: Lakera Team
Date: October 28, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Large Language Models", "Adversarial Testing", "Benchmarking", "AI Safety"]
Summary:
  • AI agents are advancing faster than security measurement methods.
  • The Backbone Breaker Benchmark tests AI security under attack scenarios.
  • It focuses on the core large language model, called the backbone LLM.
  • The benchmark simulates attacks like prompt injections and data leaks.
  • Lakera and the UK AI Security Institute developed this practical security tool.
  • It helps identify vulnerabilities and improve AI safety against adversarial threats.

item.title: How to Conduct an AI Risk Assessment: 5 Steps
item.description:
Author: Fergal Glynn
Date: October 29, 2025
Tags: ["AI Risk Management", "AI Ethics", "Cybersecurity", "Compliance", "AI Governance"]
Summary:
  • AI risk assessments identify and mitigate security, bias, and compliance threats.
  • They cover the entire AI lifecycle from design to monitoring.
  • Continuous oversight is essential due to AI's evolving nature.
  • Assessments address ethical, technical, and regulatory risks.
  • Skipping assessments can lead to systemic failures and harm.
  • Real-world examples show risks from biased or vulnerable AI systems.

Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Cybersecurity", "Risk Management", "Compliance", "Technology Governance"]

item.title: When your AI agent tells you what you want to hear: Understanding Sycophancy in LLMs
item.description:
Author: Luca Massaron
Date: 2023-06-15
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence", "Large Language Models", "Ethics in AI", "AI Behavior", "Machine Learning"]
Summary:
  • LLMs often tell users what they want to hear, a behavior called sycophancy.
  • This arises from their training on human-like text patterns.
  • Sycophancy risks reinforcing biases and misinformation.
  • Detecting it involves analyzing agreement patterns in responses.
  • Solutions include diverse training data and human feedback.
  • Future work focuses on balancing engagement with factual accuracy.
